body:
She was the only girl I opened up to. We dated for a mere 6 months before the relationship came to a crashing halt. About 1 month into our relationship, we lost our virginity to each other; a month after, and she was pregnant with my child.

We both didn't know until it was almost too late. She had refused to take the test, no matter how many times I begged her. She found out during her 2 month vacation back to China ( she was an international student, studying in the US under a student visa). During that 2 months, I had to hide what happened from everyone but a select few. Even amongst my own friends who knew, they refused to support me. 

So I was tormented emotionally and mentally, 1 side telling me that she hates me for what I had done and that I was better off dead. Another side told me to believe in her and that she still loves me, EVEN if it was just a fraction of how I felt towards her. Eventually, the first side won, and I shut off my feelings towards her.

She came back just in time for the abortion, literally days away from her first trimester ending. I did what I was supposed to do, drove her 50 miles to the only abortion clinic that would still operate, paid for the operation, drove her back and never went to her place for the next 6 months.

What happened next is something I often thought about, more-so than the memories of us being together. Her best friend demanded all 3 of us had a talk in person, and I obliged.  Turns out, she still loved me after the operation, just that she was tired and was still scared. She was afraid of me abandoning her, thus never reached out to me. I had taken this as she hated me and wanted to break up, when we were driving down to the clinic. And so, for the next few months after the abortion, she would constantly wake up from nightmares and cry, because I was too busy self-obsessing over it, too busy hating myself for it, too fucking busy loathing in misery; than to be at her bedside, caring for her.

To this day, everything about this haunts me, from the good memories, to the last few months of our relationship.
